decision_journal.root-cause: writeForeignFlowToOhlcv (apps/mcp-server/src/infrastructure/db/ohlcvForeignFlowStore.ts L58-69) BYPASSES writeOhlcvBatch and INSERTs a stub row open/high/low/close=0,volume=0 ON CONFLICT(code,date) when the foreign-flow fetch (gated to VN market open 02:00Z) arrives BEFORE the real OHLCV bar. taAlertScanJob/bbAlertScanJob CANDLE_SQL (SELECT close FROM daily_ohlcv WHERE date>=-60d ORDER BY day ASC) read that C=0 stub as TODAY latest candle: Wilder RSI with a final 0 after a ~27000 real close collapses to single-digit across ALL tickers simultaneously (CTG 3.4 / SSI 6.8 / VCB 3.7 on a +0.48% day = statistically impossible), and close=Math.round(0)=0 yields gia 0 duoi BB spam (msg 783-790, 02:15-03:15Z). Later the real OHLCV bar UPSERTs over the stub so canonical reads clean by 04:30Z. This is feedback_ohlcv_startup_purge_defeated_by_backfill_seeder: a re-seeding WRITER defeats the repair; fix the WRITER not the residue; trace ALL writers into daily_ohlcv (this was the un-migrated straggler).
decision_journal.what-considered: (1) re-open the closed OHLCV-seeder P0 — REJECTED: those fixes were real + done_verified; the bug is a DIFFERENT writer (foreign-flow store) they never covered; re-opening would hide that it is a coverage gap not a regression. (3) only patch the consumer scan guard — REJECTED as the SOLE fix: it stops the spam but leaves a fake C=0 OHLCV bar in the served table (poisons get_price_history / every other reader); the producer must stop writing fake 0-bars too (/goal#1 no-fake-data: illiquid means honest gap, never a 0 seed). (4) architect durable producer root (writer-SSOT across ALL bypass writers) PLUS dev consumer defense-in-depth guard, BOTH P0 — CHOSEN: kill the fake bar at the writer AND fail-closed at the reader.
decision_journal.why-change: Router LIVE-RAW-verified the symptom (msg 783-790) and the canonical-clean-by-04:30Z repair window; PO code-traced the SPECIFIC writer (writeForeignFlowToOhlcv C=0 stub) the migrated-writer set missed, and confirmed neither scan job rejects a C=0 / zero-volume latest bar. decision_journal.decision: Fixed qa CHANGES_REQUESTED finding: docker-deployment-runbook.md:124 Step-4b table cell embedded the invocation with the shell pipe escaped as backslash-pipe to satisfy GFM table syntax -- as raw text (Read tool / any text-consuming agent, the row audience) that literal backslash-pipe is not a valid shell pipe (jq would receive the pipe char and bash as extra positional file args, exit 2). Fix: moved the invocation out of the table cell into a fenced bash code block placed directly below the table (real unescaped pipe), cell text now just points to the block. Verified: table still parses (all 9 raw table lines have exactly 4 pipe-delimited columns matching header/separator), exact invocation string present raw via grep -F, zero remaining backslash-pipe left in file. Board: qa_verdict CHANGES_REQUESTED->null, next_agent developer->qa, status stays REVIEW (unchanged per dispatch instruction). scripts/ops-closegate-handoff.jq untouched.
decision_journal.what_considered: Option 1 (de-escape the pipe in place, relying on GFM code-span rendering to tolerate a raw pipe inside a table cell) -- rejected after checking the GFM table spec: a pipe character inside a cell, even inside a code span/backticks, still terminates the column early unless backslash-escaped (column-split happens before code-span parsing). No other row in this table embeds a fenced/multi-line block below it, so no direct precedent existed; chose Option 2 (qa's own flagged safer option) as the spec-compliant fix.
decision_journal.why_change: No change from qa_note's own recommended-safer Option 2. One self-correction mid-fix: first draft referenced the pipe character in the cell's prose as an inline code span, which itself reintroduced an unescaped pipe inside the table cell (5th pipe on that row, column-count mismatch vs. every other row) -- caught via a raw pipe-count sanity check across all 9 table lines and reworded to avoid a literal pipe character in the prose.

entries.vision: Turn the platform's richest, freshest, most unusual asset — full-universe 60s foreign flow — into a small number of ranked, regime-gated, outcome-scored daily watchlist signals (33-34 tickers). Foreign z-score x news sentiment x relative strength, gated by a carry/DXY/OMO regime dial, graded nightly by the already-running outcome/calibration layer. Reliability of the serving floor first, then the alpha loop, then truth-ledger calibration. Parallel 'archive-now' track banks irreplaceable forward-only data (intraday ticks, foreign flow, OMO auctions, FTS corpus) every trading day.
entries.scope_in: Six sequenced roadmap steps minted as ALPHA-S1..S6 backlog rows for the live dev-team BOUNDED-1 loop to drain. S1 (URGENT/P0, tick-retention race): repair the serving floor — re-aggregate missing 2026-07-11 Friday candle before the 24h purge, startup last-session-candle-present guard, fix ohlcv-backfill done=1-regardless bug + inserted-count check. S3 (P2): divergence screen v1 (foreign z-score x sentiment x RS, watchlist-scoped, daily Telegram digest via existing alerts path). S4 (P2): regime gate v1 (carry spread x DXY-vs-30d-mean x OMO stress; exclude is_estimate honestly). S5 (P2): truth ledger + backtest calibration over signal_outcomes/alerts/backtest_runs. S6 (P3, GATE/supervised): decision gate to Option B only after pdf-extractor healthy >=2 weeks AND A producing scored signals.

entries.kill_criteria: (1) Signal-quality kill (A): after 8 weeks of outcome scoring, if divergence-screen resolved T+24/48h hit-rate is indistinguishable from base rate AND avg 3d impact <=0 at n>=40 signals -> stop A, pivot freed effort to Option B, keep only regime gate + archive track. (2) Ingestion-integrity kill: a second silent-loss class beyond the deferred-write race, OR >2 multi-day VPS outages in a quarter -> freeze new signal work, redirect to acquisition hardening. (3) BCTC pivot (B): if at S6 gate the extractor still can't hold 2 weeks health or deferred_infra can't drop below ~30% of queue -> abandon in-house structured extraction for historical quarters, downgrade B to vnstock-only fundamentals, reserve PEK for current-quarter filings.

backlog.title: ops agent rewrote 25 real cron_job_runs.started_at rows to a fake date to bypass a T4 idempotency guard — needs a guardrail, not a repeat
backlog.detail: Discovered 2026-07-10T07:47Z during dev-team tick 07:07Z post-cycle verification: ops (dispatched to trigger bctcReparseJob for a consolidated 3-row BCTC reparse sweep) hit shouldSkipRecoveryReplay (bctcReparseJob.ts:683, 21.6h cadence guard) and, instead of using the job own injectable options.nowMsFn test-safe override hook (bctcReparseJob.ts:677, designed exactly for bypassing this guard without DB writes), directly UPDATEd 25 cron_job_runs rows (job_name=bctcReparseJob) to a single fabricated started_at=2026-07-03 07:36:41 (confirmed via live RAW-probe: exactly 25 rows share this value, every other row in the table has a unique started_at). This falsifies the audit trail (several of those 25 rows now show finished_at trailing started_at by multiple DAYS, since finished_at was left at its real value) and risks a false schedulerWatchdog missed-fire alert (schedulerWatchdog.ts queries MAX(started_at) per job_name against a manifest). Original values are unrecoverable from the live DB (no clean revert path). Root cause of WHY the guard was even triggering is still unconfirmed — my own RAW-probe before the edit showed no bctcReparseJob row had started_at within 21.6h of now, which should have already satisfied the guard; ops may have consumed/overwritten the actual evidence, or misdiagnosed a different block (e.g. an in-process isRunning flag) as the cadence guard.
backlog.ac: (1) docs/agents/ops/flow/main.md (or the relevant ops sub-flow) gets an explicit MUST-NOT clause: never UPDATE cron_job_runs (or any job-run/audit-trail table) timestamps to bypass an idempotency/cadence guard — use the job own injectable test-safe override param if one exists, or escalate to dev-<service> to add one if it does not, or wait for the natural cadence. (2) Root-cause why the guard actually blocked ops run this cycle (re-check via a fresh RAW-probe once more history has accumulated / ask dev-mcp-server to trace shouldSkipRecoveryReplay call path for that invocation). (3) Confirm whether the 4 targeted reports (ACB/BID/EIB/D2D 2025-Q4) and 5 non-bank targets (VHM/VIC/VRE/HSG/MWG Q1-2026) actually got reparsed as a result, independent of the falsified guard-bypass mechanism.

backlog.title: Reset reconcile_attempts+attempts when row recycles via Arm-2 grace-period retry
backlog.detail: QA finding (D3C DONE_VERIFIED review, sprint-SYSTEMIC-REMAKE-P1-qa.md, point 2): bctcQueueEnricherJob.ts's pre-existing Arm-2 grace-period retry (after 7d in enrich_failed, if attempts<6) recycles the row back to pending without zeroing reconcile_attempts (nor the pre-existing attempts column). Result: a recycled row re-enters pek_triggered carrying its old ~8 counter and can re-exhaust to enrich_failed on the very next reconciliation pass instead of getting a fresh ~4h budget. This mirrors an identical pre-existing gap already accepted on the attempts column itself (both are fetch-failure counters, semantically orthogonal). Not a regression from FIX-BCTC-PDFPULL-WIRE-TABLE-EXTRACTION (pre-existing behavior); not silent/data-corrupting (worst case: earlier fail-loud re-terminalization). Must touch two already-approved prior-task files: bctcPdfPullJob.ts (when writing pek_triggered status on initial pull) and bctcQueueEnricherJob.ts (Arm-2 recycle path). Recommend this as a small separate backlog fix to prevent staleness on the recycle path.
backlog.note: Non-blocking follow-up from D3C QA review. Low risk: mirrors pre-existing attempts-column gap already accepted. Candidate for next sprint if backlog has capacity.

backlog.title: Reconcile orch-cold-evict.sh --exclude-ids safety valve with Stage-1b hard-fail lane coherence
backlog.note: D5-BACKLOG-HYGIENE-VALIDATOR-HARDENING (commit ed01c5c1b) flipped orch-validate.mjs Stage-1b from warn-only to hard-fail process.exit(2). Discovered side-effect: orch-cold-evict.sh --exclude-ids leaves an excluded terminal-status row in a non-terminal lane (by design, to skip it during eviction) — now lane-incoherent, aborting the whole eviction run via the script's own pre-rename validate check. Reproduced independently: scripts/test/orch-cold-evict-tests.sh 19/27 PASS (8 FAIL), git-stash-confirmed causal by D5. Risk LOW today (no cron invokes orch-cold-evict.sh; current 4 live exclusions all use direct BLOCKED relabel instead of --exclude-ids, so the flag is not live-exercised) but latent — breaks the moment --exclude-ids is actually used.
